title: team_statistics silently truncates aggregation to 50 matches (default limit)
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/query.ex:14 calls matches(catalog, Map.put(filters,"team",team)) with no limit; matches/2 applies limit/2 (query.ex:134) which defaults to 50 when filters["limit"] is nil. standings (query.ex:73) and competition_statistics (query.ex:83) explicitly pass limit 100_000, but team_statistics and head_to_head (query.ex:45) do not.
suggestion: Force an unbounded limit for aggregation paths (e.g. Map.put_new(filters,"limit",1_000_000)) as standings/competition_statistics already do, so W/L/D and goals-for/against reflect the full match set, not just the 50 most recent.

title: Matches with a nil/unparseable date are excluded from ALL queries, even when no date filter is set
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/query.ex:124 `defp date?(nil, _bound, _direction), do: false` is matched before the `date?(_value, nil, _direction) -> true` clause, so match_filters?/2 (query.ex:113-114) drops any match whose normalized date is nil for from AND to filters that are themselves nil. Undated matches therefore never appear in search_matches, standings, or competition_statistics.
suggestion: Reorder clauses so a nil bound short-circuits to true regardless of the match date: only apply the date comparison when a bound is actually supplied.

title: head_to_head inherits the default limit: 50, capping the head-to-head match set
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/query.ex:45 head_to_head calls matches(catalog, filters) without a limit override; the returned games list (and thus both W/L/D records) is capped at the 50 most-recent head-to-head matches.
suggestion: Same fix as F1 — pass a large/unbounded limit on the aggregation path. Low severity because two teams rarely exceed 50 meetings in these datasets.

title: Runtime/factual probe scored 0.0 because the elixir probe only launches an escript; this solution ships an OTP app + `mix run` entrypoint
evidence: _factual.json and _runtime.json both note 'mix.exs declares no escript entrypoint'; runtime.py:682 returns None for any elixir project whose mix.exs lacks the string 'escript'. mix.exs here declares `mod: {BrazilianSoccerMcp.Application, []}` and README documents `mix run -e 'BrazilianSoccerMcp.MCP.run()'`. lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/mcp.ex implements a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server (initialize / tools/list / tools/call, 7 registered tools), so R1 is satisfied.
suggestion: This is a harness/probe expectation mismatch, not a code defect (cf. commit 28e859f1 'the factual gate was failing correct work'). Either add an escript entrypoint to mix.exs so the probe can launch it, or teach the elixir runtime probe to fall back to `mix run -e` when no escript is declared. factual_accuracy=0.0 should not be read as a functional failure of this run.
